question: The average weight of an apple in a sample of 10 apples was calculated as 104 g. Later on, it was found that the weighing had shown the weight of each apple 20 g less. The correct average weight of an apple in that sample is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each value in a data set is increased by a constant amount, the **average** of the set increases by that same amount.

Since each of the **10 apples** was **20 g** lighter than its actual weight, the **average** is also **20 g** less than the actual average.

Correct Average = Recorded Average + Error per apple

Correct Average = 104 + 20 = 124 g

**∴ The correct answer is 124 g.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of apples = 10

Observed average weight = 104 g

Weight error per apple = −20 g (under-weighed)

**Formula Used:**

Total Weight = Average Weight × Number of items

Correct Average = Correct Total Weight ÷ Number of items

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/935bffc6a146b09c4ec63d40420d091cd4408583bc67be8f20c461daa313a85f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total observed weight of 10 apples = 104 × 10 = 1040 g

⇒ Total weight error = 20 × 10 = 200 g

⇒ Actual total weight = 1040 + 200 = 1240 g

⇒ Actual average weight = 1240 ÷ 10 = 124 g

**∴ The correct answer is 124 g.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Arithmetic Operations on Average

If every observation in a data set is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant **k**, the **mean (average)** of the data set also increases, decreases, is multiplied, or divided by **k** respectively.

Correcting the Average Formula

Correct Average = [ (Observed Average × n) + (Actual value − Wrong value) ] ÷ n. This formula is useful when specific values are misread or miscalculated.

Sum of Observations

The sum of **n** observations is equal to the product of the **average** and the number of observations (**Sum = Average × n**).</p
